title: The record
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting with the subject clearly visible and centered, small-town 911 dispatch center at night and snowy suburban streets on Christmas Eve, dim console glow, cold green and deep red tones, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 3. The same 911 call, every Christmas Eve since 1952. 📼

Original fiction. Part 4 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: an officer found a dozen sets of footprints circling an empty house, and then his radio filled with singing.
scenes.image: a ring of footprints around a boarded house in snow, a candle glowing in one window

scenes.narration: Dale came back pale and silent, snow on his boots. He said the candle went out the moment he touched the door. He wouldn't say anything else.
scenes.image: a police officer sitting in a parked patrol car, snow on his shoulders, staring ahead

scenes.narration: June's shift ended at dawn on Christmas morning. She didn't go home. She went down to the basement, where the old call records are kept.
scenes.image: woman walking into a basement archive with metal shelves of old binders under a single bulb

scenes.narration: Binders back to 1990. Microfilm before that. She went back one Christmas Eve at a time.
scenes.image: a microfilm reader glowing in a dark basement, a woman leaning in close

scenes.narration: Last year. Eighteen Larkspur Road. 11:52 PM. Caller reports singing outside. The year before. Same address. Same minute. Same words.
scenes.image: close-up of stacked old binders with frayed spines on a metal shelf

scenes.narration: Every year, back to 1952. Seventy-four calls. Every one closed the same way. Nobody found.
scenes.image: rows of identical archive boxes stretching into darkness in a basement

scenes.narration: The first one was answered by a young dispatcher named Walter Hess. He quit the next morning. He bought the house on Larkspur Road.
scenes.image: vintage black and white photograph of a young man with a headset at a 1950s dispatch desk

scenes.narration: June played last night's recording, just to hear the caller again. Thin. Polite. It was Walter. Seventy-four years older.
scenes.image: woman wearing headphones in a dim basement, eyes wide, an old tape machine beside her

scenes.narration: Seventy-four Christmas Eves, one caller. And he never once got to hang up.
scenes.image: an old rotary telephone receiver resting off the hook in a dark room

scenes.narration: Then the recording kept playing, past where the line went dead. And Walter said, clearly: I'm sorry, June. I'll call you on your other line.
scenes.image: close-up of a reel-to-reel tape slowly turning in the dark, faint green light
